subject: radiology
title: Thermal ablation: planning and protection

steps.tx: Thermal ablation destroys a liver tumour with heat, and complete treatment needs a clear rim of dead tissue around the visible tumour. A **5 mm margin** around the tumour predicts complete necrosis and lowers local recurrence in examinations. **Microwave ablation** loses less energy near flowing blood than radiofrequency ablation does, so it suits tumours beside vessels. **Hydrodissection** with dextrose fluid separates bowel from the burn zone and protects the gut wall.
steps.say: Thermal ablation destroys a liver tumour with heat and needs a rim of dead tissue around it. A margin of five millimetres is important because it predicts complete necrosis and lowers recurrence. Microwave ablation loses less energy near flowing blood and suits tumours beside vessels. Dextrose fluid separates bowel from the burn zone and protects the gut wall.

steps.tx: Good imaging guides every ablation and confirms that the tumour is fully covered. **Fusion ultrasound** overlays earlier CT targets onto live liver images so the probe reaches the right spot. A contrast scan done immediately afterwards shows any residual enhancing nodule that needs further treatment. Large vessels above 3 mm cool the radiofrequency zone through the **heat sink effect**, while **general anaesthesia** keeps the diaphragm still for dome lesions.

A contrast scan afterwards shows residual enhancing tissue that needs further treatment. steps.tx: Heat can injure normal liver structures that lie close to the ablation zone. A **bile duct stricture** may follow a central burn and may need stenting for drainage. Fever after treatment may signal a **liver abscess** inside the necrotic zone and needs drainage. A **grounding pad burn** during radiofrequency treatment marks poor pad contact and needs prompt checks. Tumour seeding along the needle track remains uncommon when the track is ablated during withdrawal.
steps.say: Heat can injure normal liver structures that lie close to the ablation zone. A central burn may narrow a bile duct and may need stenting for drainage. Fever after treatment may signal an abscess and needs urgent assessment. A grounding pad burn marks poor pad contact, while track ablation during withdrawal reduces tumour seeding.

steps.tx: Follow up imaging proves whether the ablation has achieved a lasting result. **Contrast imaging at one month** with no enhancement marks technical success for the treated lesion. **Local progression** at the edge needs repeat ablation, while distant spread needs a different overall strategy. Falling **tumour markers** support the scan findings and confirm a good response. Team review aligns repeat ablation with surgery and systemic treatment options for each patient.
steps.say: Follow up imaging proves whether the ablation has achieved a lasting result. A contrast scan at one month is reassuring when no enhancement remains in the lesion. Regrowth at the edge needs repeat ablation, while distant spread needs a different strategy. Falling tumour markers support the scan findings, and team review aligns further treatment for each patient.
